additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that יגון ואנחה (grief and sighing) ARE the Sitra Achra: 'כִּי יֵשׁ יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה שֶׁהֵם הַסִּטְרָא-אָחֳרָא'. This is a bechina equation — grief and sighing share the same essential nature as the Sitra Achra; they are not merely caused by it, they ARE it. Grief and sighing refuse to serve as a merkava (vehicle/chariot) for holiness, which is the defining characteristic of the Sitra Achra. This bechina pair (יגון ואנחה ↔ סטרא אחרא) is missing from the dataset. Since the dataset has no bechina edges at all for Torah LM2/23, no package_id can be assigned; if this bechina were encoded, it would form a 2-node evil package: {יגון ואנחה, סטרא אחרא}.
additions.source_quote: כִּי יֵשׁ יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה שֶׁהֵם הַסִּטְרָא-אָחֳרָא, שֶׁאֵינָם רוֹצִים לִהְיוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה

additions.reason: The Rebbe equates שמחה (joy) with קדושה (holiness) in this Torah: bringing something into the שמחה is explicitly the same as bringing it into the קדושה — 'לְהַכְרִיחַ אוֹתָם לְהַכְנִיס אוֹתָם לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, דְּהַיְנוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה'. The word 'דְּהַיְנוּ' (meaning/that is) is the Rebbe's standard marker for a bechina equation: the Shechinah IS the joy, holiness IS joy. This makes שמחה and קדושה a bechina pair — they share the same essential domain. This missing bechina would anchor a 2-node good package: {שמחה, קדושה}.
additions.source_quote: לְהַכְרִיחַ אוֹתָם לְהַכְנִיס אוֹתָם לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, דְּהַיְנוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה, בְּעַל-כָּרְחָם

analysis_notes.notes: Torah LM2/23 has a single dataset entry for reference 1023, which is classified as type 'eitza' (not 'bechina'): 'כשאדם שמח' → 'המרה שחרה ויסורים נסתלקים מן הצד'. This causal classification is correct — when a person is joyful, melancholy withdraws. This is cause-and-effect, not parallel identity. The Torah's overall structure is a mashal (parable of forcing the sad person into the dancing circle) and its nimshal (application). The eitza logic dominates: joy causes (1) melancholy to withdraw, and at the higher level (2) melancholy itself to transform into joy. Two implicit bechinas are present in the source text that are absent from the dataset: (1) יגון ואנחה are identified as בְּחִינַת הַסִּטְרָא-אָחֳרָא — the evil counterpart package (grief/sighing = Sitra Achra); (2) שמחה is identified as the same domain as קדושה via the 'דהיינו' equation. The verse 'שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה יַשִּׂיגוּ וְנָסוּ יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה' (Isaiah 35:10) is cited as a bechina-prooftext for the entire teaching ('וְזֶה בְּחִינַת...'), but this is verse-citation usage of 'בְּחִינַת' rather than an equation between two named concept-nodes. The מרה שחרה and יסורים that appear in the eitza edge are part of the evil domain (connected to יגון ואנחה and the Sitra Achra) but are not themselves explicitly connected to each other by bechina language in the source text.
